dossiers.title: Transport Fever 2
dossiers.summary: Transport and management simulation built around creating passenger and freight networks by land, water and air. Accessible reviews emphasize logistics depth, network optimization and sandbox/modding longevity, while also noting that the systems and difficulty choices can take time to learn.

observations.statement: Reviews repeatedly value the linked passenger, freight and route-management systems as the core source of strategic depth.
Sandbox, map editing and mod support are repeatedly cited as reasons the simulation stays engaging over long campaigns.
More than one review notes that efficient freight networks and higher difficulty settings require substantial learning and planning.

dossiers.title: Arma 3
dossiers.summary: Large-scale military sandbox centered on realistic combined-arms combat, open terrain, multiplayer scenarios and extensive community-created content. Reviews consistently frame its realism and flexibility as strengths, while the slow pacing, high lethality and steep learning curve are deliberate but demanding.

observations.statement: Multiplayer, co-op scenarios and the large Workshop ecosystem are recurring reasons players describe the game as unusually long-lived.
Reviews repeatedly describe realistic ballistics, high lethality and a steep learning curve that demand patience and tactical play.
The simulation-oriented pace is repeatedly described as much slower and more deliberate than a conventional action shooter.

dossiers.title: Mutazione
dossiers.summary: Narrative adventure focused on a close-knit mutant community, relationships, gossip and a supernatural mystery, with a garden-building layer rather than combat-driven progression. The accessible review index was sparse, so the dossier relies mainly on the store description for structural characterization.

observations.statement: The game is structured around conversations, community relationships and exploration of a small settlement rather than conventional combat.
Magical gardens provide a light interactive system alongside the narrative and exploration focus.

dossiers.title: She Sees Red - Interactive Movie
dossiers.summary: Short choice-driven FMV thriller in which decisions alter scenes and lead to multiple endings. The accessible review sample highlights replaying as part of understanding the full story, which aligns with the store's emphasis on branching scenes and outcomes.

observations.statement: The interactive film uses branching choices, alternate scenes and multiple endings, making repeated playthroughs part of its intended structure.
An accessible detailed review reports that a second playthrough materially clarified the story by exposing different scenes.

dossiers.title: My Time at Sandrock
dossiers.summary: Large crafting and life-simulation RPG about rebuilding a workshop and desert town through gathering, machines, commissions, relationships and exploration. Reviews often praise the expanded systems, characters and progression compared with its predecessor, while some report bugs and comparatively clunky combat.

observations.statement: Reviews repeatedly praise the long-form workshop progression, commissions and town development as a strong engagement loop.
Character relationships and town stories are repeatedly described as a stronger part of the experience than in the predecessor.
More than one review mentions technical bugs or rough edges that can interrupt otherwise positive progression.
Combat is a secondary system and is described by some reviewers as less polished than crafting and social play.

dossiers.title: Selfloss
dossiers.summary: Atmospheric exploration and action-adventure in a Slavic-inspired fantasy world, following a healer who uses a magical staff for puzzles, traversal and combat. The accessible individual-review index was too sparse in this pass to establish recurring user-review themes.

observations.statement: The magical staff is used across combat, puzzle solving and environmental interaction, making it the central multi-purpose mechanic.
Exploration alternates between travel on foot and by boat through a melancholy fantasy setting inspired by Slavic folklore.

dossiers.title: The Gunk
dossiers.summary: Compact exploration adventure centered on vacuuming away a corrupting substance and restoring colorful alien environments. Reviews commonly find the cleaning loop satisfying and the presentation pleasant, but repeatedly note the short length, low challenge and some repetition or technical roughness.

observations.statement: Cleaning contaminated areas and watching the environment recover is repeatedly described as the game's most satisfying interaction.
Multiple reviews describe the campaign as notably short, commonly finishing in only several hours.
Several reviews characterize puzzles and combat as simple and low-pressure rather than demanding.
More than one review says the cleaning and traversal loop can become repetitive despite its initially satisfying feedback.

dossiers.title: ONE PIECE: PIRATE WARRIORS 4
dossiers.summary: Musou-style action game built around sweeping through large crowds with a broad One Piece character roster and destructible battlefields. The accessible detailed review praises the combat spectacle and roster variety but notes repetitive mission structure and a condensed story presentation.

observations.statement: The accessible detailed review praises the crowd-clearing combat and character variety as satisfying strengths.
The same review notes that mission objectives and enemy-clearing structure can become repetitive over time.
The story adapts major One Piece arcs in a condensed form rather than reproducing the full source narrative.

dossiers.title: Blair Witch
dossiers.summary: First-person psychological horror set in the Black Hills, combining exploration, story and interaction with the dog companion Bullet. Reviews often praise the oppressive atmosphere and companion relationship, while recurring criticism targets repetitive traversal, clunky interactions and moments of frustration.

observations.statement: Several reviews praise the forest atmosphere and story presentation as the strongest part of the horror experience.
More than one review reports clunky interactions, frustrating navigation or technical roughness during exploration.
More than one review describes portions of forest traversal or encounter structure as repetitive.
Bullet, the dog companion, is repeatedly singled out as an emotionally effective part of the experience.
